findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound archive members before materializing them**

When release or supply-chain tooling receives a gzip tar containing a very large regular member, this unbounded `stream.read()` materializes the member before its declared size, digest, or complete inventory is validated, allowing a compressed archive to exhaust memory instead of failing closed. Enforce per-member and total archive limits before reading content; the previous supply-chain reader's 8 MiB member bound was lost during this consolidation.

### 🛡️ Codex Security Review

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub> Security: Gate signing tags behind release approval**

If a non-release collaborator can push an `m8-007-signing-*` tag (repository tag protection is not evidenced), this runs the workflow from that tagged commit. That commit controls both this YAML and the checked-out Python while the jobs grant repository and attestation write privileges, so the collaborator can alter subjects or steps and mint Wirestack attestations without release approval. The verifier later obtains its expected source SHA from the generated hosted report rather than an independently approved revision. Require a protected release environment/ref and pin an approved commit before granting write permissions.
